provenance.text_excerpt: Together, these results indicate that (i) Sa (d17:0) can be taken up by human gut epithelial cells, then (ii) metabolized by mammalian SL-processing pathways, while (iii) inhibiting the production of mammalian C18-base SLs.

claims.statement: Bacterial-like Sa (d17:0) is taken up by human gut epithelial cells and processed by mammalian SL metabolic pathways, inhibiting production of mammalian C18-base SLs.

experiments_or_tasks: Caco-2 cells were incubated with [U–13C,15N]-labeled serine to monitor newly synthesized SLs in the presence or absence of Sa (d17:0).
Caco-2 cells were supplemented with Sa (d18:0) to stimulate de novo SL synthesis, then dosed with different amounts of Sa (d17:0).

methods.name: Caco-2 cell culture and lipid competition
methods.protocol_description: Human epithelial colorectal adenocarcinoma cells (Caco-2, ATCC) were cultured in DMEM with 10% FBS. Plates were seeded at 5×10^5 cells per 10 cm plate, incubated at 37°C with 5% CO2, and experiments took place 48 h after seeding. For lipid competition, Sa (d18:0) was added at 5 µM, and Sa (d17:0) at 0, 5, 10, and 50 µM. Cell pellets were collected after 1 h incubation.

methods.name: Metabolic labeling with [U–13C,15N]-serine
methods.protocol_description: Caco-2 cells were grown in 10% FBS in DMEM supplemented with 2.2 mM [U–13C,15N]-serine. Medium was added at the same time as 5 µM Sa (d17:0). Newly synthesized SLs were quantified at 60 and 120 minutes by measuring [M+3] labeled SLs.

methods.name: Transwell incubation with B. thetaiotaomicron
methods.protocol_description: Bacterial cells were placed on a 0.4 µM filter above Caco-2 monolayer. 50 mL cultures (OD600 0.25) grown in minimal medium with 25 µM PAA were washed and resuspended in 6 mL 10% FBS DMEM. One mL bacterial suspension was added to upper-well inserts. Contents collected after 4 h. Alkyne-containing metabolites were labeled with Alexa Fluor 647 azide using Click iT cell reaction buffer kit.
